title: War Photographer: Capture the Soldier
description: The player controls an antique camera on a tripod, rotating it to track and photograph a patrolling soldier. The soldier walks along a looping path through a battlefield scene, and the player must time their shots to capture the soldier within the camera's viewfinder at specific marked photo zones. Score points by snapping photos when the soldier is centered and in-focus.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load 'shared_assets/AntiqueCamera.glb' and 'shared_assets/soldier.glb'. Place the AntiqueCamera model at the center of the scene on a small raised platform. The soldier model should patrol a rectangular path around the scene (roughly 12 units out), using its built-in animation mixer to play its walk cycle. The camera model should rotate to follow the mouse cursor horizontally using raycasting on a ground plane, giving the player aiming control. Create a circular viewfinder overlay in the center of the screen using an HTML div with a dashed border (diameter ~200px). Place 3 glowing green ground markers (flat torus geometries) at specific points along the soldier's patrol path as 'photo zones'. Display a HUD showing: score (top-left), photos remaining out of 5 (top-right), and a flash cooldown indicator. When the player clicks, trigger a camera flash effect (brief white screen overlay fading out over 300ms) and check if the soldier's screen-space position falls within the viewfinder circle AND the soldier is near a photo zone marker. Award 100 points for a perfect shot (soldier centered + in zone), 50 for partial (soldier in viewfinder but not in zone), 0 for a miss. After each successful zone photo, that marker turns red to indicate completion. The game ends when all 5 photos are used. Show a results panel with final score and a 'Play Again' button. Set up the Three.js perspective camera at an elevated angle (y=6, z=10) looking at the antique camera. Add ambient light (intensity 0.6), a directional light simulating golden-hour sun (warm color, casting shadows), and a ground plane with a dusty brown MeshStandardMaterial. Enable shadow maps on the renderer.
